description: In most fields supervisors have the power to decide authorship contributions, and at least one first-author paper is frequently required both for the doctorate and for any subsequent post or grant.
energy_note: He decides whose name goes first on her work.

description: A culture rewarding publication counts, impact factor and authorship rank may encourage faculty to usurp credit - the 'publish or perish' structure rewarding the misconduct it produces.
energy_note: The incentive points directly at taking it.

aspect: Complaining ends the career it was for
description: The person she would complain about writes the reference, sits on the panels, and knows the editors. Being right is not protective.
energy_note: Winning the argument ends the reason for having it.

description: 'I've put myself first on this one - it'll travel further with my name on it, which helps you.' She designed it, ran it and wrote it. He is not entirely wrong about it travelling further, and that is what makes it impossible.
energy_note: Robbed, with an argument that is partly true.

aspect: The catalogue of supervisory misconduct is forty years old
description: Goodyear, Crego and Johnston's study had psychologists describe 144 ethically problematic incidents in research supervision, identifying incompetent supervision, supervision abandonment, abusive and exploitative supervision, dual relationships and encouragement to fraud.
